heard: A moon of Saturn zaps passing spacecraft with static electricity. Most moons are just solid spheres of ice. Saturn's moon Hyperion is a sponge, half as dense as water. Over 40% of its interior is totally empty space. When meteorites hit, they punch inward, crushing the icy foam. Gravitational tugs from Titan make Hyperion tumble through space uncontrollably. As it tumbles, Hyperion builds up a negative 200 volt charge. As NASA's Cassini probe flew past, Hyperion fired a beam of electrons. It proves a moon of Saturn zaps passing spacecraft with static electricity.
